<MethodEndpoint
  method={"get"}
  path={"/resource-types/{type}/resources"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



Filter by the `query.filters` defined for the type. `parentId` is the root of a Resource subtree. Use the Open `deviceId` for Device nodes, and the exact node ID for other nodes. `page` defaults to `1`. `pageSize` defaults to `20` and has a maximum of `100`. `sort` uses declared fields with `:asc`/`:desc`. The response does not include `total`; use `hasMore` instead. Network/Device/Point entries return the protocol type in `properties.protocolId`. Device IDs are not duplicated in `properties`. References returned by create or import must be read again for details. Undeclared filter parameters return `400`. `parentId` applies only to types that declare it. `sort` defaults to `id:asc`.

When querying `type=sequence`:
- If `deviceId` is omitted, the user-defined sequence library is returned.
- If `deviceId` is provided, only scenes already owned by that device are returned by default, including bound user configurations, device presets, and system built-ins. Entries that already belong to the current device include `properties.assignment`.
- If `includeAssignable=true`, the response also includes unbound, capability-matched user scenes that are available for selection and do not have `properties.assignment`. If the parameter is omitted or set to `false`, assignable scenes are not returned. If `deviceId` is omitted, this parameter is ignored.
- For built-in scenes, `properties.name` and `properties.labelTypeName` return localized text based on the `Lang` request header.
- When `deviceId` is provided, the response `data` echoes `deviceId` and the device `spec` as `data.deviceId`/`data.spec`.
